prompt: Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserving animation key poses. Make a production sprite atlas for an offline children's learning app. Polished friendly storybook animal illustration with soft shaded fur/feathers/scales, clear anatomy and expressive eyes, matching the reference style. ONE animal identity reused in ALL cells, camera/head size/body proportions/markings EXACTLY consistent. Every pose is full body, no cropped limbs. All face RIGHT unless subject says front-facing. Genuine transparent background, NO coloured paper/background, floor, panels, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, speech bubbles, motion lines, cast shadows or decorative objects. Equal square grid cells with 8% safe margins, consistent scale, same notional ground baseline 85% down each cell for grounded poses. The top LEFT cell is frame1 and order is row-major. Carefully articulate actual jaws/legs/wings/tails; do NOT simply rotate/scale the entire animal as a substitute.  Layout 2 columns by 2 rows, 4 poses; overall SQUARE canvas, square cells. All empty pixels alpha ZERO, no paper or grid. Reference is STYLE ONLY, not rabbit anatomy/colours. A friendly full-body generic grey SHARK with white underside, clear gill slits, tall dorsal fin, paired pectoral fins and a vertical asymmetrical tail; not a dolphin (no mammal blowhole or horizontal flukes). FOUR SWIM poses: body level facing RIGHT, tail bends left, tail crosses centre, tail bends right, returns. Head/eye/body stay the same shape and scale, true tail-driven swimming. Rounded child-friendly teeth only if mouth visible. No water (runtime supplies it).
